institutional_domains.title: Stronger statistical research discipline: multiple-testing control, regime-segmented validation, and decay monitoring

gaps: Multiple-testing guard exists but is not currently green.
next_actions: Add a multiple-testing guard artifact that records hypothesis families, correction method, and false-discovery limits for each research batch.
Add decay-monitor reports by lane and regime so promoted bots can be retired before forward performance silently erodes.

institutional_domains.title: Formal model governance: approvals, champion/challenger, rollback bundles, and promotion committees in code
institutional_domains.summary: Champion/challenger, promotion gates, lifecycle hygiene, and rollback entry points are real, but governance is still mostly operator-centric rather than committee- and approval-workflow-driven.
gaps: Rollback exists, but there is not yet a fully bundled promotion packet with committee metadata and deployment attestations.
next_actions: Add committee-style promotion packets that capture reviewers, rationale, rollback bundle hashes, and deployment approvals.
Treat champion/challenger transitions as signed governance events with mandatory approval metadata.

institutional_domains.title: Security and compliance hardening: RBAC, secret rotation, tamper-evident audit logs, and strict paper/live separation
institutional_domains.summary: Secrets scanning, audit journaling, RBAC, and paper/live separation are now represented as first-class controls, but the repo still needs stronger freshness and live-ops compliance discipline to look institutional.
next_actions: Add an RBAC manifest for live actions, promotion approvals, deletion lanes, and emergency controls.
Promote secret-rotation and audit-journal freshness into a dedicated security control-plane artifact.

institutional_domains.title: Deeper reliability engineering: restore drills, chaos testing, machine-independent deployment, and queue durability
institutional_domains.summary: Reliability is one of the stronger parts of the system thanks to watchdogs, restore drills, and maintenance lanes, but machine-independent deployment and explicit chaos drills still need work.
next_actions: Add scheduled chaos drills for writer loss, storage path failover, and stale-artifact lane failure.
Publish a machine-independent deployment bundle so restore drills can be replayed off-host with the same runtime contract.

institutional_domains.title: Better observability: SLOs, paging rules, incident timelines, cost telemetry, and golden-signal dashboards
institutional_domains.summary: The system already has good operator-facing health summaries and SLO guards, but cost telemetry and a fuller incident-timeline surface still need strengthening.
next_actions: Add cost telemetry for market data, storage, training, and sidecar backend usage into the operator dashboard.
Publish an incident timeline artifact that stitches alerts, watchdog actions, and operator interventions into one review surface.

institutional_domains.title: Team-grade developer process: CI gates, schema contracts, migration discipline, code owners, and runbooks
institutional_domains.summary: CI, commands, runbooks, schema tracking, CODEOWNERS, and a migration manifest are now in the repo, but the process still needs stricter team enforcement to feel institutional.
next_actions: Add CODEOWNERS and ownership policy for strategy, risk, ops, and storage subsystems.
Introduce migration manifests for schema changes, artifact version bumps, and replay compatibility changes.

point_in_time_data_lineage.title: Point-in-time data lineage and a true feature store
point_in_time_data_lineage.summary: Lineage hashes, event-store normalization, training snapshots, and a feature-store manifest now exist, but point-in-time serving and governance contracts still need tightening.
next_actions: Publish a canonical feature-store manifest with dataset partitions, join keys, and effective-time windows.
Promote snapshot coverage into a required point-in-time completeness gate before retrain and promotion.

immutable_experiment_tracking.title: Immutable experiment tracking with dataset/model hashes and exact replayability
immutable_experiment_tracking.summary: Experiment tracking is now hash-centric, but exact replayability still depends on the latest recorded bundle being complete and the replay hash registry staying green.
gaps: No immutable experiment-registry row is available yet.
No append-only immutable experiment-ledger summary exists yet.
next_actions: Record experiment rows with dataset, model, and replay hashes for every training and promotion candidate, not just session starts/stops.
Keep replay hash registry healthy before promotion so immutable replay expectations stay anchored.

high_fidelity_simulator.title: A much higher-fidelity simulator: queue position, partial fills, cancels, borrow, fees, venue rules, and latency
high_fidelity_simulator.summary: The simulator now exposes queue position, partial fills, cancel probability, borrow drag, fee drag, venue penalties, and latency, but it still needs deeper venue-specific market microstructure to feel institutional.
next_actions: Add venue-specific fill models for opening auctions, halts, and partial-cancel behavior by broker and market.
Promote simulator telemetry into replay and paper-performance reports so model research sees queue/cancel/borrow drag directly.

portfolio_construction.title: A real portfolio-construction layer above the signal bots: netting, factor controls, capacity, exposure budgets
portfolio_construction.summary: Portfolio risk and execution budgets exist, but the portfolio layer is still mostly budget- and exposure-oriented rather than a full factor- and capacity-aware allocator.
gaps: There is no evidence of a factor-neutral or optimizer-driven portfolio construction layer yet.
next_actions: Add a portfolio allocator that nets sleeve intents and enforces factor, sector, and regime exposure budgets before orders are emitted.
Introduce per-symbol and per-venue capacity curves so portfolio construction can reason about crowding and execution impact.

independent_risk_services.title: Independent pre-trade and post-trade risk services that are not embedded in the strategy path
independent_risk_services.summary: The repo has meaningful pre-trade and post-trade safety services, but they are still tightly coupled to the same codebase and do not yet look like separately deployable risk services.
gaps: Pre-trade and post-trade controls still live inside the main repo rather than as separately isolated services with independent deploy surfaces.
Risk-service evidence is stronger on limits and reconciliation than on truly independent service boundaries.
next_actions: Split pre-trade approval and post-trade reconciliation into independent service endpoints with their own deploy and audit surfaces.
Publish risk-service contracts so strategies cannot bypass portfolio, execution-budget, or reconciliation checks.

transaction_cost_and_capacity.title: Better transaction-cost and capacity models by symbol, venue, and time of day

next_actions: Add capacity curves by symbol, venue, and clock bucket so research and execution budgets share the same cost model.
Promote TCA breakdowns into paper and replay artifacts by venue, order type, and volatility regime.
